title: introduce hardware-affinity metadata, sharded changelog generator, and microprofile snapshots
author: Elena Park
description:
Motivation: Different inference hardware (a100, h100, triton-hosted tensorrt, amd-gpu) show materially different optimal kernel/quantization choices and recommended batch sizing. Customers and model owners currently store a single 'performance profile' per model which conflates these hardware differences and makes changelogs noisy when we update heuristics. This PR introduces a lightweight 'hardware_affinity' field in the onboarding metadata schema, a migration to split existing profiles into microprofiles keyed by affinity, and a sharded changelog generator that emits per-affinity release notes to make rollouts and triage clearer.

What I changed: 1) schema/registry/model.yaml: add optional hardware_affinity map (recommended keys: cpu, a100, h100, trt, amd). The map contains profile hints (quantize: int8/float16, kernels: [fused_attn, flash_attn], batch_hint, kv_cache_opt). 2) onboard/migrations/20251112_split_profiles_by_affinity.py: migration that converts legacy single-profile models into per-affinity microprofiles using heuristics (fallback strategy != breaking). 3) tools/changelog/shard_by_affinity.py: new generator that reads release deltas and writes separate changelog fragments per affinity, plus an aggregate summary. 4) tests/test_affinity_profile.py: unit tests for schema validation and migration. 5) docs/onboarding/hardware-affinity.md: docs for model owners and SRE explaining how to write affinity-aware profiles and interpret per-affinity changelogs. 6) examples/sample-onboard-affinity.json: example metadata demonstrating multi-affinity entries.

Checklist: - [x] Schema addition with open/optional field and backwards-compatible defaults - [x] Migration script with dry-run mode and a safety flag --apply-once - [x] Unit tests covering edge cases (missing affinity, unknown hardware) - [x] Changelog generator integrated with existing release pipeline (writes fragments to artifacts/) - [x] Docs and example metadata - [ ] E2E profiling job to validate suggested kernels (tracked in follow-up ENG-3492)

Compatibility and migration notes: The hardware_affinity field is optional. When absent, runtime will consult the legacy profile (unchanged). Migration attempts to create best-effort microprofiles but leaves a single 'legacy' profile for models where heuristics can't confidently split. The migration includes flags to run in dry mode and an idempotent marker so it can be rolled out safely on production registries.

Performance impact: No runtime behavior change unless customers opt-in to affinity-specific routing or we enable affinity-aware defaults. The sharded changelog reduces human noise for release engineers and should speed triage when regressions are reported only on specific hardware.

Rollout plan: 1) Merge schema + migration and ship as behind-feature-flag for the console. 2) Run migration in dry mode across staging and gather sample microprofiles (2 weeks). 3) Enable migration --apply-once for low-risk namespaces, run validation jobs. 4) Switch release pipeline to include per-affinity fragments and update release notes workflow docs.

Related work: ENG-3150 (affinity routing prototype), ENG-3293 (changelog pipeline refactor).
